Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Zephyr Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Zephyr Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Johnathan Hale, CEO; Sarah Kline, CFO; Mike Thornton, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Reflecting on Q3, we are proud of the significant strides Zephyr Motors has made across all facets of our business. We have achieved remarkable progress in total revenue growth, software and services monetization, electric vehicle range enhancements and efficiency improvements, forward guidance, capital investments, margin expansion, strategic priorities, and the effects of our pricing actions. The market reception to our Zephyr Apex SUV has been overwhelmingly positive, with the associated demand surge far exceeding our initial estimates.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline to discuss our financial performance in greater detail.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. Let's start with the top line. For the third quarter ended September 30, 2024, Zephyr Motors reported total revenue of $2.82 billion, representing a robust 48% year-over-year increase from $1.91 billion in Q3 2023. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of triple-digit YoY growth in automotive revenues and reflects the successful ramp-up of our second-generation platform, including the Zephyr Apex SUV and Zephyr Pulse sedan, which together accounted for over 70% of our vehicle deliveries this quarter.

Breaking it down by key revenue segments, which align with our vertically integrated model encompassing vehicles, energy solutions, and regulatory credits—a playbook tailored to our premium mid-market positioning against competitors like Rivian and Lucid. Automotive revenues, which comprised 87% of total at $2.45 billion, surged 52% YoY. This was propelled by record vehicle deliveries of 28,500 units, up 55% from 18,400 units last year. Average selling price, or ASP, held steady at $82,000 per vehicle, benefiting from a favorable mix shift toward our higher-margin Apex SUV, now at 45% of mix versus 30% a year ago. Pricing discipline amid softening demand in some segments was key; we avoided the aggressive discounts seen from legacy OEMs like Ford with the Mustang Mach-E or GM's Equinox EV, preserving brand value.

Our regulatory credits revenue jumped to $210 million, a 120% YoY increase, driven by ZCA—Zephyr Credit Agreements—sales to non-compliant automakers scrambling under tightening CAFE standards and EU CO2 regulations. With our zero-emission fleet multiplier at 1.45x under the IRA, we outperformed peers like Stellantis, which reported credit shortfalls last quarter. This segment now contributes a healthy 7.5% to total revenue, providing non-dilutive cash flow to fund our Nevada Gigafactory Phase 2 expansion.

Energy generation and storage revenues grew to $140 million, up 35% YoY, fueled by deployments of our Zephyr PowerPack 400 kWh modules. We shipped 1.2 GWh this quarter, including a landmark 500 MWh deal with a major California utility for grid stabilization—akin to Tesla's Megapack wins but optimized for our LFP-NMC hybrid chemistry, which delivers 15% higher cycle life at a 20% lower cost per kWh. Services and other revenues rounded out at $30 million, up 25%, from OTA software upgrades and our growing SuperCharge network, now at 450 stalls across North America.

Regionally, North America drove 62% of revenues at $1.75 billion, up 60% YoY, turbocharged by IRA Section 30D credits averaging $7,500 per vehicle and the $4,000 30C point-of-sale rebates. Deliveries here hit 18,000 units, with the Apex SUV capturing 12% market share in the $70K-$90K SUV segment, outpacing Rivian's R1S. Europe contributed 22% or $620 million, growing 40% despite 25% EU tariffs on Chinese imports like BYD's Atto 3, which shielded our Dusseldorf plant output of 6,200 units. ASPs here rose 8% to €78,000 on stronger demand for our CCS2-compliant models amid the phase-out of BEV subsidies in Germany.

China and APAC made up 12% at $340 million, up 25% YoY but moderating from prior quarters due to fierce local competition from CATL-powered NIO ET7s and XPeng G9s. Our Shanghai JV with a local battery supplier enabled 4,300 deliveries, leveraging GB/T fast-charging standards and our new 800V architecture for 10-80% charges in 18 minutes—a spec matching Xiaomi's SU7 but with superior ADAS via our Zephyr NeuralDrive Level 3 autonomy stack.

Key trends include a 28% YoY reduction in COGS per vehicle to $58,000, driven by our in-house 4680 cell production at the Nevada Gigafactory, now yielding 95% first-pass efficiency. This incorporates silicon anodes for 12% higher energy density, directly boosting range to 420 miles EPA on the Pulse sedan. Supply chain resilience was critical; strategic LFP sourcing from CATL mitigated lithium price volatility, which spiked 15% in Q3 amid Andean mine disruptions.

Before moving on, I'd like to highlight our software and services revenue, which continues to be the crown jewel of our high-margin, recurring revenue model. In Q3, this segment delivered $512 million in revenue, representing a staggering 142% year-over-year growth and now accounting for 9.2% of our total quarterly revenue. This marks the fifth consecutive quarter where software outpaced our automotive hardware growth, underscoring our transition from a pure-play EV manufacturer to a tech-driven mobility platform—with our unique edge in edge-AI compute and fleet-scale data loops.

Subscriptions and connectivity services were our largest bucket at $348 million, up 158% YoY, fueled by an expanding installed base of 2.8 million connected vehicles—that's 92% attachment rate on our cumulative deliveries of 3.05 million Zephyr EVs and crossovers to date. Our ZephyrLink Premium suite, which includes OTA map updates, in-car entertainment powered by our proprietary ZephyrOS, and advanced driver assistance features, generated an average revenue per user of $12.50 per month, with churn under 1.2%—best-in-class, thanks to our gamified loyalty program that rewards safe driving with free feature unlocks.

North America led with $212 million, or 61% of the segment, driven by high uptake in urban markets like California and Texas, where 65% of our subscribers opt for the full bundle. In China, we're at $98 million, or 28%, growing 210% YoY on the back of our Shanghai Gigafactory ramp and partnerships with Baidu for localized HD mapping. Europe contributed $38 million, tempered by slower Level 2+ adoption due to stringent UNECE regs, but we're optimistic with our Berlin pilot for ZephyrLink Ultra, which bundles V2G charging optimization for the EU's Green Deal incentives.

Autonomous driving revenue hit $164 million, up 112% YoY, comprising robotaxi usage fees, enterprise licensing, and beta Full Autonomy subscriptions. We've now logged over 450 million autonomous miles across our fleet, training our neural nets on our in-house Vulcan supercluster—a 10-exaflop beast—which has slashed inference latency by 40% for our Level 3-capable ZephyrPilot system. Key wins: In Q3, we launched commercial robotaxi operations in Austin and Shenzhen, generating $72 million from 15,000 daily rides at $0.85 per mile—25% below Waymo's pricing, with 98.9% uptime. Our FA beta, priced at $199/month for early adopters, reached 285,000 subscribers, or 12% of eligible fleet, with a 78% conversion rate from supervised FSD trials. Margins here are exceptional at 87% gross, versus 62% for automotive.

Strategically, we're accelerating with fleet-scale data moat from 1.2 TB/day of edge-collected data, giving us a 3x edge in rare-event prediction; bundling and upselling where 42% of new vehicle buyers pre-subscribe to a 3-year FA bundle, boosting lifetime value to $18,500 per vehicle from software alone; and B2B expansion like deals with Uber Freight for 5,000 Zephyr Semi autonomy kits and Hyundai for white-label ZephyrPilot licensing. Software ARPU is tracking to $15 by year-end as we roll out ZephyrRide hailing and predictive maintenance services. With Q4 deliveries guidance at 32,000 units, we expect software to hit $650-700 million, pushing full-year to $2.1 billion—a 155% YoY jump.

Turning to gross margins, our automotive gross margin came in at 22.4%, up 410 basis points year-over-year from 18.3%, and up 120 basis points sequentially from 21.2%. Excluding regulatory credits, which contributed about 2.8 points, our core automotive margin expanded to 19.6%, reflecting the strength of our underlying cost structure. Favorable product mix accounted for roughly 150 basis points of expansion. Shipments of our premium Atlas SUV and the new mid-cycle refresh of our Bolt-X crossover represented 58% of total volume, up from 42% a year ago. These higher ASP vehicles carry richer margins.

COGS trends are encouraging: per-vehicle COGS declined 14% YoY to $41,200, driven by battery cost deflation—cells are 38% of total COGS. We've transitioned 65% of North American production to in-house 4680 cylindrical cells at Gigafactory Ohio, delivering a 28% cost-per-kWh reduction versus legacy LG suppliers. LFP cells for China-sourced models are down to $92/kWh from $132/kWh, while NMC packs hit $105/kWh through Panasonic partnerships and structural battery pack designs. Ohio Giga is running at 92% capacity, and we've realized $450 million in material cost savings through supplier consolidation—now at 85% localization in North America.

Regionally, North America hit 25.1% margins, bolstered by IRA-compliant content unlocking $1,200 per vehicle in incentives. Europe saw 18.9% due to subsidy phase-outs, but we're countering with price hikes and OTA upgrades. Asia-Pacific delivered 20.3%, offset by JVs. Over eight quarters, margins have stair-stepped from mid-teens to low-20s, targeting 25% core by year-end 2025 via vertical integration to 85% in-house batteries, platform synergies, recurring revenue from Horizon Autonomy at 90% margins, and supply chain resilience.

On pricing strategies and promotions, in a competitive landscape with Tesla's Model Y adjustments and BYD's sub-$10,000 Qin Plus, our global ASP was $48,200, down 8% YoY due to promotional pricing and volume trims. This drove 15% sequential volume growth to 185,000 units and $8.9 billion in automotive revenue, up 12% YoY, but contracted margins by 220 bps to 18.4% as discounts averaged 7.5% off MSRP.

Our dynamic pricing via VoltEdge analytics adjusted MSRPs like $2,500 on AeroSedan to $39,800 effective ATP. In North America, Summer Surge shaved $3,000 off fleet orders, reducing inventory to 38 days. Europe’s Green Drive leasing at €299/month drove 35% uptake. China rebates captured 4.2% share. Promotions like zero-APR, VoltLoyal trade-ins, and FluxFlex subscriptions lifted share to 7.1% globally, with 2.5x ROI. Q4 pilots include algorithmic pricing and 4680 integration for sustainable cuts.

For guidance, we expect Q4 automotive deliveries at 32,000 units and reaffirm full-year 2024 revenue of $10.8-$11.2 billion, implying 50%+ growth. Gross margins track to 22% for the year. Looking to Q1 2025, revenue of $5.8 billion to $6.2 billion, 25% sequential growth, and full-year 2025 of $24 billion to $26 billion, 60-70% increase. Vehicle sales ~$5.0-$5.3 billion from 85,000-95,000 deliveries at $52,000-$55,000 ASP. Energy $650-$750 million, services $150 million. North America $3.5-3.8 billion, Europe $1.4-1.5 billion, APAC $900-$950 million. Margins 21-23% on vehicles.

On capex, for FY2024 we're on track for $12.8 billion, up 15% YoY, 8.5% of revenue. FY2025 $14.5-15.5 billion to support 2.5 million capacity by 2026. Manufacturing 45% or $5.8 billion: Nevada Phase 3 $1.5 billion for 100 GWh 4680s, Spartanburg $1.2 billion, Cologne $800 million. Batteries 30% $3.8 billion: solid-state $900 million, sodium-ion $500 million, recycling $400 million. Product dev 20% $2.6 billion: Gen4 $1.4 billion, FSD $800 million. Supply chain 5% $640 million for semis and SuperCharge. ROI-disciplined at 20%+ IRR.

Our financial position remains strong, with ample cash reserves. We anticipate solid performance for the upcoming quarter.

Next, we'll hear from Mike Thornton regarding the latest developments in our manufacturing operations.

Mike Thornton:
Thank you, Sarah. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at optimal levels to meet the surging demand for our vehicles. We have successfully implemented advanced automation technologies, resulting in increased production output and reduced cycle times. At Gigafactory Nevada, Phase 2 is yielding high-efficiency 4680 cells at 95% first-pass, supporting our scale-to-sustain initiative with a third assembly line for 100,000 annual capacity by Q2 2025. Ohio Giga hits 92% utilization, and we're retrofitting for next-gen platforms, ensuring just-in-time inventory at lean levels.

Following me, Dr. Elena Vasquez will provide an update on our technological innovations.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. Our R&D team is relentlessly pursuing breakthroughs in battery technology, autonomous driving systems, and vehicle connectivity. Range anxiety remains the biggest barrier to EV adoption, cited by 68% of potential buyers per J.D. Power. We've achieved an average EPA-rated range uplift of 18% YoY across our portfolio, to 412 miles fleet-wide. The 2023 Apex sedan now delivers 485 miles, a 22% improvement, via 800V architecture and 112 kWh packs at 285 Wh/kg. Efficiency down to 168 Wh/mile, 14% better than Q4 2023, leading Tesla Model Y and Rivian R1S.

OTA efficiency suite to 85% of fleet adds 7-9% range via adaptive thermal management and 92% regen recapture. Real-world data from 1.2 million vehicles shows 12% lower energy use. Battery tech scales 46-series cells with silicon anodes to 98% of packs, 22% higher density, 1,500 cycles. Aerodynamics at Cd 0.198, 97.2% powertrain efficiency, low RR tires. Nevada Phase 2 yields 50 GWh, compressing battery BOM 19% to $85/kWh.

In North America, 92% qualify for IRA >300-mile credits, 14% share in $50K+ segment. Europe WLTP 620 km on Terra SUV, 42% sales surge. China 550 km CLTC. Roadmap: 500-mile EPA by 2026 via semi-solid-state at 300 Wh/kg. This boosts ASPs $2,100/unit, cuts warranty costs.

After me, Raj Patel will offer insights into our supply chain strategies.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Elena. We have established a resilient and diversified supply chain network to mitigate risks and ensure the seamless flow of materials. Our proactive approach has navigated global challenges, with strategic LFP from CATL, cathode diversification to Redwood Materials, and 85% NA localization. Offtakes like Umicore for 20 GWh reduce Asian reliance. Critical minerals hedging covers lithium volatility, and recycling hits 95% recovery for EU regs. SuperCharge to 15,000 stalls supports utilization.

Next, Lisa Chen will share updates on our sales performance and market expansion initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Raj. Our sales team has achieved remarkable success in expanding our market reach and driving revenue growth. We are seeing strong demand across regions, with Apex SUV at 12% NA share, 28% YoY growth. Fleet deals with Amazon/UPS, leasing in Europe, subscriptions in China. Backlog at 85k, inventory 15 days. Q1 targeting 25% fleet share via V2G, India entry via Tata JV.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Mark Thompson with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Sarah, can you expand on the revenue breakdown and what drove the 48% growth? Also, how sustainable is the regulatory credits piece?

Sarah Kline:
Sure, Mark. As I detailed, automotive was the powerhouse at $2.45 billion, up 52%, from 28,500 deliveries and steady $82k ASP on Apex mix. Credits at $210 million are sustainable given tightening regs and our 1.45x multiplier—peers like Stellantis are short. Energy and services added high-margin layers. Regional strength in NA from IRA, Europe tariffs helping us. This momentum, with COGS down 28% to $58k via 4680s, sets up continued outperformance.

Operator:
Next question from Emily Chen at Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Great, thanks. On software revenue, that's impressive growth. Can you talk more about ARPU trends and robotaxi ramp?

Sarah Kline:
Absolutely, Emily. Subscriptions at $348 million drove it, with $12.50 ARPU on 2.8 million connected vehicles, low churn via loyalty. Autonomy $164 million from Austin/Shenzhen robotaxis at $0.85/mile and 285k FA betas. Data moat from 450 million miles on Vulcan cluster enables Level 4 by H1 2025. B2B like Uber Freight adds run-rate. Expect $15 ARPU year-end, $2.1 billion full-year.

Operator:
Our next question from David Lee, JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:
Mike, on manufacturing, how are you addressing capacity for Q4 guidance, and utilization trends?

Mike Thornton:
David, Nevada Gigafactory at 95% OEE on 4680s, adding third line for 100k capacity Q2 2025. Ohio 92%, Spartanburg ramping. Scale-to-sustain $1.2 billion capex funds this, with just-in-time keeping inventory at 8,500 units, down 30% YoY. Automation cuts cycle times, ready for 32k Q4 deliveries.

Operator:
Next from Sophia Grant, Barclays.

Analyst 4:
Elena, impressive range gains. How do these impact competitiveness versus Tesla/Rivian, and roadmap details?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Sophia, 412 miles fleet average, 485 on Apex beats Model Y/R1S efficiency. Silicon anodes, Cd 0.198, 97.2% motors deliver real-world 320 miles NA. Tailored WLTP/CLTC regionally. Semi-solid-state to 500 miles 2026, DOE cryogenic cooling. Adds $2,100 ASP, lower TCO $0.18/mile vs ICE.

Operator:
From Robert Kim, Citi.

Analyst 5:
Raj, supply chain risks with lithium volatility—how diversified now?

Raj Patel:
Robert, LFP from CATL, manganese cathodes from Redwood, Umicore offtake. 40ktpa lithium from Pilbara, 70% hedged. 85% NA localization, recycling 95%. Shields from Andean disruptions, positions for IRA/EU regs.

Operator:
Last from one before additional, Laura Evans, Deutsche Bank.

Analyst 6:
Lisa, sales outlook with pricing pressures—how's demand pipeline?

Lisa Chen:
Laura, strong with 85k backlog, Apex 12% share. Promotions like zero-APR boosted conquest 18% from ICE. Fleet 25% Q1 via V2G. China share up via rebates, Europe leasing. Inventory 42 days global.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Operator:
Next from Tom Reilly, RBC.

Analyst 7:
Johnathan, strategic priorities for 2025—Gen4 launch and autonomy?

Johnathan Hale:
Tom, Q1 ramp to 40k units, 24% margins. FY2025 480-520k deliveries, $14-15B revenue, 27-29% margins. Gen4 Apex Max truck H1, 500-mile, $52k targeting pickups. Solid-state $65/kWh, FSD beta Q2 on 5B miles, robotaxi Austin Q4. Vans, luxury, India JV. Net-zero 2027.

Operator:
Final question from Karen Walsh, BlackRock.

Analyst 8:
Sarah, capex details and margin trajectory risks?

Sarah Kline:
Karen, $12.8B FY24, $14.5-15.5B FY25. 45% manufacturing like Nevada 100 GWh, 30% batteries solid-state/sodium-ion. Targets $70/kWh, 25% margins 2025. Risks hedged: lithium volatility, IRA stable with 40% US content. Vertical 65% moat.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. As we look ahead, our priorities center on ramping production, refining costs, regional execution, platform acceleration, verticalization, autonomy monetization, diversification, and sustainability. We're scaling from disruptor to leader, confident in delivering exceptional results and long-term value for shareholders. We look forward to sharing progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Zephyr Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
